tagline.text: A watershed reserve behind Cebu City with Kan-irag trekking trails

location.label: Location
location.text: Central Cebu highlands (parts of Cebu City, Toledo, Talisay, Danao and more)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,500 (per person per day, covering round-trip motorcycle taxi, entrance fee, food and drinks)

children.text: Central Cebu Protected Landscape is a watershed reserve of about 29,062 hectares in the mountains behind Cebu City. It offers easy viewpoint and camping outings at Kan-irag Nature Park and Sirao Peak, while rules for some trekking routes are still being drawn up, so check before you go.
Central Cebu Protected Landscape (CCPL) is a protected area that spans the mountains and drainage basins in the middle of Cebu Island. It covers about
29,062 hectares

and includes parts of Cebu City, Toledo, Talisay and Danao, plus parts of Balamban, Minglanilla, Consolacion, Liloan and Compostela. It was declared a national park in 1937, became a protected landscape on August 12, 2003 under Proclamation No. 441, and Republic Act No. 9486 in 2007 defined its component areas.

Before it is a tourist destination, this is the source of water for Cebu City and nearby cities. Its components are the former Central Cebu National Park, the Buhisan Dam area, the Mananga Watershed Forest Reserve, the Kotkot-Lusaran Watershed Forest Reserve and Sudlon National Park. Officials have repeatedly warned that losing the forest would bring water shortages and a higher risk of floods, which is why it matters so much to people in Cebu.
The easiest way in for visitors is Kan-irag Nature Park and Sirao Peak in the hills north of Cebu City. It takes about
40 minutes
from downtown by car or motorcycle taxi, and rewards you with cool air, ridge views and camping. It pairs well with Sirao Flower Garden or Tops Lookout for a one-day outing.

That said, this is not an open leisure park like a beach resort. Management and rules differ from zone to zone, and in autumn 2026 a popular trail on the Buhisan side was closed while new trekking rules are being drafted. This guide sticks to confirmed facts, so check the latest announcements before you leave and find out which activities are allowed in each zone. For first-time visitors it works as a light half-day nature outing from Cebu City, and for residents and long-stay travelers as a weekend camping and birdwatching spot. If you expect a national park with fixed visiting hours and a well-equipped information center, you may be disappointed, so set your expectations accordingly.

blocks.title: Cebu's water tank: about 29,062 hectares of watershed forest

children.text: The whole landscape is a watershed that supports household, farming and industrial water use in Metro Cebu. The forest also acts as a natural barrier against soil erosion and floods. The reason to visit is less a single dramatic photo than the chance to feel what this forest means. The landscape is managed by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources Region 7 (DENR-7), and the Protected Area Management Board (PAMB) holds authority over biodiversity and watershed conservation.
This nature park of about
71 hectares

in the Cebu City highlands opened in the mid-2000s. Native trees were planted on what was once a bald mountain, turning it back into a watershed forest, and about 27 native bird species have been recorded. The entrance fee used to be about

, but the information is old, so confirm locally. The park is described as having a reception area, restrooms and rest huts, with trails marked by stones. Alcohol, firearms and pets were listed as prohibited.
You can camp on a ridge at about
above sea level with cool views. As of a 2023 guide, entrance and camping cost about
, and the summit is closed because of the landowner, so only the campsite below the summit is available.

blocks.title: Buhisan Dam and Buhisan Watershed Forest Reserve

children.text: Buhisan Dam is about

high and was built starting in January 1911 and completed on February 11, 1912, as the starting point of Cebu's waterworks. A ceremony marked its 100th anniversary in 2012. The area around the dam is a water source, so unrestricted entry is limited.

President Quezon proclaimed it a national park on April 11, 1936, and it lies in the Sudlon district on the edge of Cebu City. It is also a historic site where the last stronghold of Cebuano revolutionary forces stood during the Philippine-American War. Information for ordinary visitors is scarce, so confirm details before going.

The Cebu flowerpecker, a critically endangered bird, was rediscovered in 1992 in a limestone forest in Tabunan inside this landscape. The black shama, streak-breasted bulbul and Philippine tube-nosed fruit bat also live here. For birdwatching, walk quietly and move at dawn. The Cebu flowerpecker is a small bird about
long with a very limited range, so ordinary travelers have little chance of seeing it. At Kan-irag, though, you can meet common native birds such as the emerald dove and the olive-backed sunbird.

blocks.title: Mount Manunggal and the western Cebu highlands

children.text: Mount Manunggal, the third highest peak in Cebu, is known for a route that starts on the Balamban side, and a route from Tabunan in Cebu City is also described as a main trail. It is famous as the site of the 1957 crash of President Magsaysay's plane and is covered in detail as a separate entry.
This trail, about
5 km

long, has been closed since September 21, 2026. The reason was spray-painted graffiti found on trees, boulders and check dams inside the Buhisan area. If this is the trail you are planning to hike, first check whether it is open.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: Kan-irag Nature Park and the Sirao area

children.text: Leave Cebu City. With a car, head up toward Busay and follow the old Sirao golf course road. By public transport, take a jeepney or bus to JY Square in Lahug and switch to a motorcycle taxi.
Walk the marked trail at Kan-irag Nature Park and take in the ridge views from the viewpoints. Confirm locally before you go whether it is open and what the entrance fee is.
Move on toward the Sirao Peak campsite to enjoy the views and rest. The summit is closed, so go only as far as the campsite.
Have lunch at a restaurant near Sirao Flower Garden or Tops Lookout and head back to the city.
Motorcycle taxis climb steep, winding roads, so bring a helmet and comfortable shoes. The road gets slippery in the rain, so it is safer to go on a dry-season morning.
Arrive at the campsite, pick a tent spot and ask staff about the rules. Always get permission before lighting a bonfire.
Watch the sunset and the Cebu City night view from the ridge. Nights are cool.
Enjoy the dawn birdsong and sunrise, then pack out all your trash and head down.
Weekends can be crowded and noisy. For quiet camping, choose a weekday.
Leave Cebu City at dawn and head up toward Kan-irag. Birds are most active early in the morning.
Walk the marked trail slowly and watch the forest edge and the water. Binoculars help, and keep your voice low.
Before it gets hot, rest at a ridge viewpoint and drink water.
Come down the mountain, have lunch in the city and rest.
Weekdays have fewer visitors, so you can enjoy the birds and scenery in peace. Be even more careful to confirm whether the site is open.
A nonstop flight from Manila's Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Mactan-Cebu International Airport takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
on average (1 hour 20 minutes to 1 hour 40 minutes depending on the flight). Several airlines fly the route, so compare prices when booking.
From the airport to central Cebu City, take a taxi or Grab. Depending on traffic it takes about
40 minutes to 1 hour

items.title: From Cebu City to Kan-irag and Sirao

children.text: It is about
18 km
from the Cebu City Capitol, and takes about
40 minutes
by car or motorcycle. The slopes and curves are steep, so make sure your vehicle can handle them.
By public transport, take a jeepney or bus to JY Square in Lahug and then a motorcycle taxi. As of a 2023 guide, the fare was about
from JY Square and about
from the Plaza Housing side.
Sudlon and Buhisan are in the hills southwest of Cebu City. It is hard to reach the entrances by ordinary public transport, so use a taxi, a rental car or a local guide.
One guide says that for Sudlon National Park you get off at the junction and walk about
1 km
to the entrance. The source is old, so confirm locally.

The best time for trekking and camping is the drier period from December to May. Nights are cool and clear then, which is good for views. Dawn and dusk are the coolest times to walk, while midday can be hot because there is little shade even along the ridge.
From June to November it rains often, trails get slippery and streams can rise suddenly. During this period, avoid stream crossings and camping.

Staying in central Cebu City or around IT Park and going up for the day is the easiest approach. If you want to spend a night on the mountain, you can use a tent or hut at the Sirao Peak campsite, but facilities and rates can change, so ask in advance.

There are few restaurants on the mountain, so prepare food and water before you go up. Near Sirao Flower Garden and Tops Lookout there are restaurants and cafes that are handy on the way down. If you bring a packed lunch, take all food waste back with you. This is a protected area where many spots have no trash bins, and wild animals can be drawn by the smell of food.
Before you leave, check with the CCPL Protected Area Management Office (PAMO) or the Cebu City environment office about which sections are open and whether a permit is needed.
Bring at least
2 liters
of water, plus electrolyte drinks and energy snacks. This is a protected area, so carry all your trash out.
Pack trekking shoes, long pants and a wide-brimmed hat, and a waterproof bag in case of rain.
Trails branch in many directions and some have poor signs, so a guide is recommended. Stay within sight of your group.
On a motorcycle taxi, wear a helmet and agree on the round-trip fare and waiting time before you set off.
When watching birds, do not get too close and keep the noise down. Do not feed animals or pick plants.
Always get permission on site before camping or lighting a fire, and note that spray-painting or damaging facilities can lead to legal action.
Mobile signal is weak in places on the mountain, so download maps in advance and bring a power bank.

The Spartan Trail has been closed since September 21, 2026, and entering the closed section can lead to investigation and legal action. New trekking rules were under consultation in November 2026, so be sure to check the latest announcements.
Whether trekking and camping are allowed inside the protected area depends on the management zone (multiple use zone or strict protection zone).
There are several entrances and exits, which makes monitoring difficult, and some have no warning signs, so you need to check the rules yourself.
Streams rise sharply when it rains, so avoid river crossings in the rainy season.
Trails have few signs and it is easy to get lost. Do not go alone, and let someone know your plans.
Entrance fees, facilities and opening hours differ between blogs and travel sites and may differ on site.
Watch out for insects, leeches and snakes, and bring long clothing and first-aid supplies.
A flower garden a short drive from Sirao Peak, popular for mountain views and photos. See its separate entry for prices and hours.
A Cebu City night-view lookout that one guide says is about
10 minutes
from Kan-irag.
A Taoist temple in the Busay hills that pairs well with a mountain drive.
Once you come down from the protected landscape, you can explore the city's churches, fort and markets.
